what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: What the corpus of record lost while we were away
agents.why: Our own safety check is refusing the newest corpus. Two things it can no longer name: three of the eleven sector families, and the written eligibility rules for fifteen funds. The second one matters most — that text is what makes a fund readable to the AI, and making rows readable was one of the biggest wins we have had, so losing it quietly undoes shipped work. The half-finished answer from before the interruption has been recovered and says the sectors are a column that is empty in one copy rather than rows that vanished. This finishes it, and says whether a founder feels any of it today.

agents.what: A thousand encoded rules the two copies disagree about
agents.why: The corpus of record holds about 1,070 fewer encoded eligibility rules than the working copy — a 14% gap, larger than either thing the safety check actually caught, and it caught neither of them. Those rules are the one thing measured to tell apart two funds from the same programme, which is where two thirds of our misses turn out to be. So this asks three things: are the two copies even counting the same thing, what does the gap cost if it is real, and what the check should have done — it has already been fooled twice in this family, once crying wolf and once staying silent while work was thrown away.
